# Tangential acoustic rigidity of the transformed invariant quartic cone

Date: 9 November 2026.
Status: author-derived analytic candidate. No independent review, numerical search, scientific execution, general quasiconvexity solution, or historical-priority claim is made.

## 1. Question and answer at the earned scope

Can the original anisotropic planar quartic J_r in Astra N1496 be certified merely by positive combinations and coefficientwise limits of arbitrary invertible left/right coordinate transforms of the full bi-rotational rank-one-convex quartic cone?

The answer is NO for every r>0. This includes the entire cone covered by Bruno and Pasqualotto, arXiv:2608.06367v1, Theorem 2 and Appendix A, not just the Dacorogna--Marcellini one-parameter subfamily. The obstruction survives singular-transform limits, arbitrary positive mixtures and coefficientwise closure.

This is a certificate-class exclusion. It does not show that J_r is not quasiconvex. It does not settle the unrestricted original normal-coupling problem. The source itself reports r=1 as an already proved quasiconvex control, so a negative Jensen interpretation would be particularly wrong.

## 2. Exact cone

For F in R^(2x2), set s(F)=|F|_F^2 and d(F)=det F. Define

  W_t(F)=s(F)^2+4t s(F)d(F)+(6t^2-2)d(F)^2,  -1<=t<=1.

The primary theorem gives the complete bi-SO(2)-invariant rank-one-convex homogeneous quartic cone:

  Q(F)=a s(F)^2+b s(F)d(F)+c d(F)^2,
  a>0, |b|<=4a, c>=-2a+3b^2/(8a),

or a=b=0,c>=0. Equivalently,

  Q=a W_t+mu d^2, t=b/(4a), mu>=0.

The primary also proves these Q are quasiconvex. We use its algebraic cone characterization; the exclusion below does not require importing its quasiconvexity proof.

Let C be the coefficientwise closed positive conic hull of Q(L F R), for all such Q and all real invertible L,R. Coefficients are in the finite-dimensional vector space of real homogeneous quartics in the four entries of F.

Invertible left/right transformations preserve quasiconvexity: use a linear change of target and domain in the defining gradient inequality. Positive sums preserve it, and coefficientwise convergence preserves each fixed compactly supported test integral. Hence C is a legitimate sufficient quasiconvexity cone, provided the primary theorem is accepted.

# Prior and uncertainty

## Direct primary comparisons

1. Jan Kristensen, On the non-locality of quasiconvexity, Annales IHP C 16 (1999), 1–13.
   https://www.numdam.org/item/AIHPC_1999__16_1_1_0.pdf
   Definitions on pp.3–4 distinguish small-gradient weak quasiconvexity from agreement with a globally quasiconvex function nearby. Proposition1 gives the classical strict Legendre-Hadamard case. The present contribution addresses degenerate contacts, not that ordinary case.

2. Bruno–Pasqualotto, Quasiconvexity for the Dacorogna–Marcellini Energy, arXiv:2608.06367v1.
   https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06367v1
   Its global bi-SO(2) quartic theorem and heat/exact-form method are strong prior. The symmetry class differs from the original one-sided invariant J_r. No automatic transfer is claimed.

3. Sergio Gutierrez, A Necessary Condition for the Quasiconvexity of Polynomials of Degree Four, Journal of Convex Analysis13 (2006), 51–60.
   https://journalofconvexanalysis.com/articles/jca13004/jca13004.pdf?v=2
   The reviewed cubic acoustic cancellations and resonant necessary conditions are relevant antecedents. The inspected statements do not supply the current sufficient bound for every compatible small-gradient test.

4. Bandeira–Pedregal, Quasiconvexity: the quadratic case revisited, and some consequences for fourth-degree polynomials (2008).
   https://matematicas.uclm.es/omeva/wp-content/preprints/preprint10-08.pdf
   Independently read during review; its Fourier characterization and quartic criteria concern zero-mean questions rather than the specific full-rank degenerate-background radius.

5. Agazzi et al., Sharp Higher Integrability Theory Part I: The Lp-norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform, arXiv:2609.28311v2 (8 October 2026).
   https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28311v2
   Theorem1 and Corollary2 state global Burkholder quasiconvexity and sharp Beurling norms; Lemma4 uses projection onto a convex scalar-gradient constraint. The displayed primary theorem/proof was read during final packaging, but not independently audited here. No automatic transfer to the anisotropic original J_r is established. It is a potentially stronger global method comparison, not a dependency of the present proof or a historical novelty clearance.
